title: Create a release manifest for a project
description: Write a `release-manifest.json` for a single project — author, project identity, release commit, date, and version. The file lands at the project root; it is up to each project's build to copy it into the output.

examples.description: Writes `<web-root>/release-manifest.json` using the local git user name and the current timestamp.
Writes `<shared-types-root>/release-manifest.json` with an explicit release date.

project.description: The workspace project to generate the manifest for.
project.x-prompt: Which project is the release manifest for?

version.description: Semantic version written to the manifest as `version`. Pass it positionally — `nx` reserves `--version` as a named flag.

releaseCommit.description: The commit being released, written to the manifest verbatim. A short hash is recommended.
releaseCommit.x-prompt: Which commit is being released? (short hash recommended)

releaseDate.description: Release timestamp. Any value `Date` can parse is accepted and normalized to an ISO 8601 UTC string. Defaults to the current date and time.

author.description: Release author. Defaults to `<git user name> (<git user email>)`, dropping the email when it is not configured. Omitted from the manifest entirely when no name can be resolved.

dirPath.description: Output directory for the manifest, relative to the project root. Defaults to the project root itself.
